hypothesis: organicScore below minOrganicScore identifies low-quality tokens in the traded age window
motivation: the gate was rejecting every candidate
sample_source: decision_snapshots in the live observe corpus
metric: fraction of tokens with organicScore greater than zero
result: 0 of 461 - the provider has not computed the score at that age
action_taken: changed from an unconditional hard veto to a hard veto only when the score has been computed and a 0.25 soft-risk term when it has not
notes: A gate that rejects 100 percent of the population the strategy is defined over is measuring data availability and not token quality. The change does not weaken the rule for tokens that have a score.

hypothesis: devBalancePercentage above maxDevBalancePct identifies creator-dump risk
motivation: the gate was rejecting the great majority of candidates
sample_source: decision_snapshots in the live observe corpus
sample_window: tokens inside the configured age window
metric: fraction of tokens where the field is absent
action_taken: changed to a hard veto only when the field is present and a 0.20 soft-risk term when it is absent
notes: Same class of error as MT001 and corrected the same way. A value that is present and bad remains an unconditional refusal.

motivation: the figure counts the liquidity pool as a holder

result: not a valid measurement of holder concentration before migration

motivation: the term reads organicScore which MT001 showed is structurally zero across the traded age window
metric: contribution of the organic term to the composite score
result: structurally zero for the entire eligible window
action_taken: none yet - the term still carries weight 0.20

hypothesis: minLiquidityUsd is set at a level that admits tradeable tokens and excludes untradeable ones
motivation: the floor was chosen a priori and has never been measured
metric: round-trip loss as a function of provider-reported liquidity
result: 8 of 10 closed positions exited via exit_cost_exploded meaning exit price impact breached maxExitImpactBps rather than price moving against the thesis
action_taken: none - the configured value stands unmodified
notes: First evidence against the floor but n=10 from one session is not a sample. Recorded so that any later change to minLiquidityUsd is visibly motivated by these outcomes and therefore outcome-driven requiring a hold-out. Raising the floor until these exits disappear would be fitting the threshold to the ten observations that prompted it.

result: chosen from a constraint not from data

motivation: caps must be chosen before evidence exists

notes: Risk caps are a constraint and not a hypothesis. Loosening one is a hypothesis and requires its own row.

hypothesis: lossBps reports a strictly nonzero value whenever value changed
result: false - a change smaller than before divided by 10^7 truncates to exactly zero
action_taken: the property was corrected to the true claim and the resolution floor was documented on the function
notes: Recorded because a rejected hypothesis about our own code is exactly what this ledger is for. The test was wrong and the code was right.

hypothesis: positions are entered at a size the exit liquidity cannot support
motivation: 8 of 10 closed paper positions were forced out by maxExitImpactBps rather than by price
metric: share of closed positions whose exit reason is exit_cost_exploded
result: superseded - the 8 are two populations not one. 4 were total liquidity collapse (final sell impact -9900 to -10000 bps and ~0 SOL returned) and 4 were ordinary cost drift (+519 to +911 bps with roughly the entry amount returned). paper.ts:360 applies Math.abs so both record the same reason
action_taken: none - logged as an observation and registered as defects Q029 and Q030 before any threshold is contemplated
notes: The original framing was wrong because it trusted the exit_reason column. Only about 4 of 10 are evidence about entry sizing or the liquidity floor; the other 4 are rugs that no exit rule could have salvaged. Corrected the same day it was written. Any threshold change motivated by this still requires a hold-out.

hypothesis: an exit outcome can be defined over executable sell output instead of over a provider's priceImpactPct field
motivation: 8 of the first 10 closed paper positions carried one exit reason that spanned a token evaporating to 13 lamports and a position that was up 5.7% of cost
sample_source: position_exits backfilled from the stored quote and fill corpus
metric: number of distinct economic events sharing a single exit label
result: one label split into three unrelated outcomes: 4 liquidity_collapse, 4 cost_drift, 1 severe_exit_degradation, 1 ordinary_stop_loss
action_taken: maxExitImpactBps removed from ExitConfig and replaced by liquidityCollapseRatioBps stated over executable value; historical rows reclassified under exit-accounting-v1
notes: Not a tuning. The old knob was defined over a field for which Jupiter documents no sign convention (checked 2026-08-12), so no threshold over it had a stable meaning. The replacement is not fitted to outcomes and does not appear in any entry decision. COLLAPSE_RATIO 0.10 is a definition of where 'how much did we lose' becomes 'is there a market at all', chosen before looking at where the corpus fell; the four collapses landed at 0.0000 to 0.0094 and the nearest survivor at 0.4703, so no value in [0.01, 0.47] would separate them differently.

hypothesis: the take-profit rule has never fired because it is unsatisfiable, not because no position qualified
motivation: a boundary test written for take_profit failed; inspection showed gain measured with lossBps(mark, cost) then tested as -up >= takeProfitBps, which is false for all inputs
metric: counterfactual net result of positions that exceeded takeProfitBps at some observed mark
result: 1 of 10 positions (39bb459b) exceeded 6000bps at mark 13 of 19 and exited at mark 19 for -0.007073668 SOL; corrected rule closes it at +0.033411329 SOL from its own stored marks
action_taken: argument order corrected to lossBps(cost, mark); a reachability test and two boundary tests added
notes: takeProfitBps itself is UNCHANGED at 6000. This row exists because fixing an unreachable rule changes realised behaviour even though no threshold moved, and because the +0.0334 figure was computed after looking at the corpus. It is a single position and is not evidence of edge. The four liquidity collapses show a counterfactual delta of ~0.0000 SOL, so the corrected collapse rule rescues none of them at the 31s mark cadence.

hypothesis: the paper daily loss cap censors the sample precisely after losses, biasing any expectancy estimate upward
motivation: paper mode stopped entering after 4 collapses realised -0.109 SOL against a 0.06 SOL cap. Trades are then missing NOT at random - they are missing exactly after losing sequences - so the surviving sample over-represents days that started with wins. For a phase whose entire purpose is unbiased estimation of expectancy that is a defect in the instrument, the same class as O039. Separately, the cap made P8 own preregistered 200-closed-trade gate unreachable: at ~2 entries per day it is a 100-day run
metric: entries refused with reason daily_loss_cap while below maxSimultaneousPositions
result: every entry attempt refused for ~16h; 145 eligible candidates, 0 open positions, 0 trades added to the sample
action_taken: paper dailyLossCapLamports 0.06 -> 0.5 SOL. canary (0.02) and live (0.06) UNCHANGED. drawdownHaltPct implemented and set to 50 for paper as the enforced backstop that replaces the throttling the cap was doing by accident
independent_confirmation: not applicable - this is not a strategy threshold and it does not change which tokens are entered, only how many trades per day the instrument records
notes: This IS a loosening of an enforced risk cap and is recorded as one. Justification is that paper mode holds no capital, so the cap protects nothing there and only shapes the sample; canary and live keep their tight values, and the drawdown halt (previously declared and enforced by nothing - see O040) now bounds total paper loss at 50 percent of NAV. Deliberately NOT changed: any entry gate, the liquidity floor, position size, or any exit threshold. Distinguish this from an outcome-driven change - no return figure motivated it and none was improved by it

hypothesis: a declared drawdown halt that no code reads is indistinguishable from no drawdown halt
motivation: drawdownHaltPct sat in RiskConfigSchema and in SAFER_WHEN_LOWER - the tree would refuse to loosen it - while no module read the value. It is also a preregistered P8 canary gate (max drawdown <= 10 percent of paper NAV), so the readiness report would have been computed against a limit nothing enforced
result: zero, across all packages and apps
action_taken: implemented as the drawdown_halt refusal in sizePosition, measured against peak NAV replayed from close order rather than starting NAV; paper value set to 50
independent_confirmation: 5 unit tests including both boundary sides and a peak-vs-start discrimination test
notes: Effective behaviour goes from unbounded to bounded at 50 percent, which is a strict TIGHTENING of what the code actually did, even though the number in the file rose from 6. The three remaining dead halts (maxAggregatePlannedLossPct, dailyLossHaltPct, weeklyLossHaltPct) are unimplemented and are a named canary blocker in docs/READINESS.md, not a silent gap
